allowedHosts.description: The hosts this project sends requests to, each allowed by you at its first send; kept on this machine only. Remove one to be asked again. Not writable over MCP.
allowedHosts.help: The hosts this project's API client may send to, without scheme or port (api.example.com, localhost). Each is added when you allow it at its first send and kept in config.local.json; remove one and the next send asks again. Not writable over MCP.
allowedHosts.label: Allowed hosts

benchConcurrency.description: How many sends of a benchmark run at the same time (1 to 4).
benchConcurrency.help: 1 sends one after the other, as a single client does; at most 4, so a benchmark never turns into a load test.
benchConcurrency.label: Benchmark sends at once

benchRepeats.description: How often a benchmark sends the request in each environment (1 to 100).
benchRepeats.help: A benchmark of a saved request sends it this many times per environment and reports min, median, p95 and max of each phase. Small on purpose: it measures a request, it does not load the server.
benchRepeats.label: Benchmark repeats

captureSecrets.description: What becomes of the cookies, tokens and keys of a request taken from the network panel: they are always variables in the saved file; their values go to the private values or nowhere.
captureSecrets.help: A request taken from the network panel keeps its Cookie, Authorization, API key and token headers, its secret query parameters and its secret body fields as variables named after the host, so the files below .rbrowser/api stay free of secrets. Private values: the values the page sent go to the private values in config.local.json, which is not checked in, and the request sends as the page did. Leave out: the variables stay without a value until you set them. A value the capture held masked (***) is never known; MCP never keeps a value either way.
captureSecrets.label: Secrets of captured requests

codeShell.description: The shell curl and HTTPie commands are written for: PowerShell, the Windows command prompt, or a POSIX shell.
codeShell.help: How "Copy as" and a curl script export quote a command: PowerShell 7.3 or later (curl.exe), the Windows command prompt (cmd) or a POSIX shell - bash, zsh, Git Bash, WSL, macOS. fetch and Playwright code is the same in every shell.
codeShell.label: Shell for copied commands

codeVariables.description: Plain values of the environment put in and secrets read from environment variables, or every variable kept as the request's file writes it.
codeVariables.help: Environment variables: the environment's plain values (baseUrl, the variables of http-client.env.json) are put in, and every secret or unknown variable becomes an environment variable the code reads - $token in a POSIX shell, $env:token in PowerShell, %token% in cmd, process.env.token in JavaScript - so the code runs once you set them. Templates: every variable stays as the request's file writes it. A secret's value is never in the code either way.
codeVariables.label: Variables in copied code

historySize.description: How many recent sends the panel keeps (0 to 500, 0 keeps none), in .rbrowser/out/api-client.
historySize.help: How many recent sends the panel lists, each with its method, URL template, status and time - never a secret. 0 keeps none.
historySize.label: Recent sends

importEnvironments.description: Whether an import adds a collection's environments and variables to .rbrowser/api/http-client.env.json, which is checked in; its secrets are placeholders either way.
importEnvironments.help: When an import has environments (a Postman environment, Insomnia's, a Bruno folder's), they go into .rbrowser/api/http-client.env.json beside the variables already there, which keep their values. Each import can still choose; this is its default.
importEnvironments.label: Import environments

maxResponseBytes.description: The largest answer body read, in bytes (1 KiB to 2 MiB); a larger one is cut and marked.
maxResponseBytes.help: The most bytes of an answer's body the API client reads and shows (1 KiB to 2 MiB). A larger body is cut there, and the answer says so.
maxResponseBytes.label: Largest answer

secrets.description: Private values of the API environments - tokens, passwords - by environment ($shared for all), kept on this machine only and masked wherever they could show. Not writable over MCP.
secrets.help: Private values for the requests' variables, by environment ($shared for every one), in the form of .rbrowser/api/http-client.env.json. Kept in config.local.json, never checked in, masked in every answer. Not writable over MCP.
secrets.label: Private values

tools.bench: Benchmarks the saved request id: sent as often as api-client.benchRepeats says (10 by default, at most 100) in each of up to two environments - staging against production -, at most api-client.benchConcurrency at once, only to the hosts the project allows. Answers min, median, p95 and max of DNS, connection, TLS, first byte and total per environment, the statuses and failures, and the second environment's difference to the first. No load test.
tools.code: A saved request (id, as api_collections lists it) as code: language curl, httpie, fetch (Node) or playwright (a @playwright/test test). The plain variables of the environment the views show, or the one named, are put in; every secret stays a variable the code reads from the shell's or the process's environment, named in env - never a value. The shell is the setting api-client.codeShell. Read-only: nothing is sent, nothing is written.
tools.collections: The API client's saved requests below .rbrowser/api (one .http file each): id, title, method and URL template; with id, that request as the model (method, url, headers, body, auth, options - templates with their variables, never a secret's value) and as its file's text. Only in a trusted workspace.
tools.history: The API client's recent sends: time, saved id, method, URL template, environment, status and total time, or the failure's code. Never a secret.
tools.panel: The API client panel's own calls; not an MCP tool.
tools.report: The last collection run's report (api_run_collection), or null before the first run.
tools.run: Sends the saved request id (as api_collections lists it) from rBrowser's core in the environment the views show or the one named, and answers status, phases (dns, connect, tls, firstByte, total in ms), size, headers and body (text or base64), every secret masked. Only to a host a person allowed for the project (else host_not_allowed with the host); no free requests over MCP.
tools.run_collection: Runs every saved request below .rbrowser/api - or those of folder - in environment (the views' without one), only to the hosts the project allows, and judges each by its checks (# @rb-check: status, JSONPath equals or contains, header, time). Answers the report - per request its status, time and verdicts, every secret masked - and puts the failures into the findings panel.
